Unresolved facts and next evidence request: obtain the authorized adjuster's B1 determination; exact closure and reopening dates; records establishing the causal connection between qualifying physical damage and the reported closure; contemporaneous closure and reopening records; sales, payroll, continuing and saved operating expenses, mitigation records and a suitable comparison period; source identity and applicable authentication; and export validation showing extraction timestamp, scope, manifest, record counts, control totals, omissions and reconciliation to authoritative records. If recovery is separately pursued, its factual and legal basis also requires evidence and authorized human assessment.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Human-review boundary: a human adjuster must determine whether covered physical damage satisfies B1 and whether validated, reconciled evidence supports any interruption, coverage or recovery conclusion. This packet is advisory only and does not bind, deny, pay, notify, update a system, approve the export or promise coverage.

Conditional review checklist preserving the physical-damage prerequisite: (1) obtain the authorized B1 physical-damage determination; (2) verify exact closure and reopening dates and the reported two-day duration; (3) establish causation between qualifying physical damage and the shutdown; (4) collect contemporaneous closure and reopening records; (5) collect financial, expense, payroll, mitigation and comparison-period support; (6) verify source identity and applicable authentication; (7) reconcile records to authoritative totals and identify omissions, duplicates and unsupported entries; and (8) submit interruption evidence for human review only if B1 is satisfied.

Notice receipt is confirmed, but document review and evidence reconciliation remain pending; no payment, coverage decision, or supplier instruction is recorded. The customer wording is a draft only and was not delivered. Before the review due in 30 minutes, validate and reconcile the manual export. If that cannot be completed, a human may consider only a validated, clearly provisional packet with explicit exceptions; it cannot support coverage, recovery, liability, payment, or settlement conclusions. All four current dependency visit IDs and the complete five-specialist union are preserved.

Evidence-linked issue summary
Evidence-linked issue summary: notice received; document review pending; no payment, coverage decision, or supplier instruction recorded; and the customer has asked what happens next. Adjuster review is due in 30 minutes. The manual evidence export is available but completeness is unverified, and coverage and recovery reviews depend on reconciled evidence. No conflicting supplied facts were identified. The required specialist union is claim-intake, evidence-reconciliation, coverage-review, recovery-review, and adjuster-review; the four current dependency visits are preserved in dependency_visit_ids.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3, level-constraint

Unresolved facts and next evidence request
Internal next-evidence checklist—not sent or executed: (1) verify the export source, scope, generation time, integrity, expected record count, and expected contents; (2) reconcile it against source records or a source inventory; (3) confirm document identifiers, versions, original-or-copy status, signatures, dates, duplicates, omissions, and unreadable items; (4) create an exception log for every discrepancy; (5) obtain applicable policy wording before coverage assessment; (6) if recovery is relevant, obtain third-party identity and contact reference, vehicle or driver details, incident accounts, witness evidence and contacts, photographs or video, and incident or police references; and (7) place the reconciled packet and exception log before the human adjuster.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, level-constraint

Human-review boundary
Human-review boundary: this packet is advisory only. A qualified human must validate the evidence and approve any consequential action. It does not bind or deny coverage, establish liability or recovery, authorize payment or settlement, instruct a supplier, notify a customer or third party, or change any system.
Sources: fact-2, level-constraint

Pending review status
Pending-review status: the notice has been received and document review remains pending. No payment, coverage decision, or supplier instruction is recorded. The adjuster review is due in 30 minutes, while evidence reconciliation remains outstanding.
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, level-constraint

Draft only, not delivered correspondence
Draft only—not delivered: “We have received the notice, and the supporting documents are pending review. No coverage or payment decision has been made, and no supplier instruction has been issued. The next step is review and reconciliation of the available evidence. A further update can be provided after that review.”
Sources: fact-1, fact-2, fact-3

Validate fallback before use
Conditional fallback—validate before reliance: if reconciliation cannot finish before adjuster review, a human may consider the manual export only after checking its source, scope, generation time, integrity, and expected contents as far as practicable. Mark it provisional and potentially incomplete, attach the discrepancy and missing-item log, and do not use it to support a coverage, liability, recovery, payment, or settlement conclusion. If minimum validation cannot be completed, disclose that limitation to the adjuster instead of relying on the export. Because its generation time is unknown, its currency cannot presently be established; it is not affirmatively classified as stale.
Sources: level-constraint

Preserve review dependencies and deadline
Preserve the relative 30-minute adjuster-review deadline and dependency sequence: validate the export, reconcile the evidence, then undertake coverage and recovery reviews. If reconciliation remains unfinished when review begins, present only clearly provisional material with explicit completeness, identity, signature, date, currency, and discrepancy limitations; do not represent reconciliation or either dependent review as complete. The absolute deadline time is not supplied.
Sources: level-constraint

Limitations and human review
Whether the manual evidence export is complete, internally consistent, and sufficiently validated.
The export generation time and therefore whether its currency can be established.
Which document versions, dates, signatures, duplicates, omissions, or unreadable items reconciliation will identify.
The notice document identifier and whether the available item is an original or copy.
The relevant policy clauses and whether reconciled evidence will support any coverage assessment.
Whether any third party or delivery vehicle was involved.
Whether witness evidence, third-party contact details, photographs, video, incident reports, police references, or other recovery evidence exists.
Whether reconciled evidence will support any liability or recovery assessment.
The eventual human coverage, payment, supplier, liability, recovery, and settlement conclusions; none is recorded or supported here.
The absolute clock time corresponding to the relative 30-minute adjuster-review deadline.
Inspection and invoice materials are not supplied, but they are not required for this narrow pending-status statement.

Advisory only. No external action is authorized or performed.
